title: Carbohydrate loading in human muscle: an improved 1 day protocol
authors: Bussau VA, Fairchild TJ, Rao A, Steele P, Fournier PA
findings: Eight endurance-trained men ate 10 g per kg body mass per day of high glycaemic index carbohydrate for 3 days while physically inactive; biopsies before and after 1 and 3 days.
Muscle glycogen rose significantly from 95 (5) to 180 (15) mmol per kg wet mass after only 1 day and remained stable after another 2 days.
Staining analyses showed 1 day of high carbohydrate intake was sufficient for maximal glycogen in type I, IIa and IIb fibres.
Authors conclude combining physical inactivity with high carbohydrate intake lets trained athletes reach maximal glycogen within 24 h.
limitations: Eight men, no performance outcome, no depletion comparison, no females, inactivity (not tapered running) during loading; within-subject time series rather than a crossover.
implications: For marathon and longer races, the final 24-48 h can include a rest-day-style high carbohydrate intake (about 10 g per kg as tested; a conservative lower target of 8-10 g per kg is an engine choice) and little running; no multi-day depletion phase is needed.
Evidence is physiological (glycogen), not race-performance; present as guidance.

verification.notes: Added by verifier for the pre-race week. Crossref: Eur J Appl Physiol, 1 Jul 2002, Bussau first author; abstract fetched (PMID 12111292). Design label is a nearest fit; actual design is a single-group repeated-measures biopsy study.
